thread.title: Tech Today: Apple’s Low-Profit Services, Souring on Facebook, Tesla Hits Pause - Barron's

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Tech Today: Apple’s Low-Profit Services, Souring on Facebook, Tesla Hits Pause - Barron's
text:
By Tiernan Ray Updated April 17, 2018 10:55 a.m. ET Here are some things going on today in the world of tech :
Shares of Netflix ( NFLX ) are up $21.46, or 7%, at $329.24, adding to last night’s gains, after the company yesterday beat Q1 revenue and profit expectations, on comfortably higher subscriber gains, and also beat with its outlook for this quarter.
Price targets are zooming into the high $300s to the $400 range this morning.
The sell side is focused on the company’s better-than-expected international subscriber additions.
And the verbiage is glowing from most analysts.
Evercore ISI ’s Vihay Jayant notes subscriber growth is “accelerating globally,” calling Netflix “La Casa de Subscribers.”
KeyBanc’s Andy Hargreaves concludes the results show the “investment efficiency” of its programming.
R.W. Baird ’s William Power calls it “alternated reality,” and says the company’s “zooming into the future,” and poses the question, “ Can anything slow its subscriber momentum?”
The company is “making a habit of delivering strong results,” writes Piper Jaffray ’s Michael Olson.
J.P. Morgan ’s Doug Anmuth says the company "Makes its Case for the Best Global, Secular Growth Story in Tech."
Some Sour on Facebook
This week’s Barron’s magazine features an interview I did with tech stock manager Ken Allen of T. Rowe Price , who runs the T. Rowe Price Science and Technology fund ( PRSCX ), and who is very bullish on Facebook ( FB ), calling it a great company that’s suddenly on sale.
The Wall Street Journal ’s Michael Wursthorn reported late yesterday that some large funds are giving up on Facebook. He cites Brad Slingerlend of the Janus Henderson Global Technology Fund, which has began reducing its stake in Facebook before the scandals broke out. Slingerlend tells Wursthorn the stock may need to come down further.
Other wary funds are Vontobel Asset Management and Copper Rock Capital Partners LLC.
Facebook stock this morning is up $2.60, or 1.6%, at $167.43.
Tesla Temporarily Halts Model 3
The bad rumors are back for Tesla ( TSLA ). Buzzfeed ’s Caroline O’Donovan late yesterday wrote that the assembly line for the company’s “ Model 3 ” sedan has been halted, a sudden four- to five-day production “pause,” she writes, with employees being told to take action days or “stay home without pay.” O’Donovan cites a Tesla spokesperson as saying the company’s working on “improving automation” as the reason for the pause.
Tesla stock is down $4.41, or 1.5%, at $286.80.
Apple Music’s Low Profit
Ben Schachter with Macquarie Research this morning reiterates his Outperform rating on Apple ( AAPL ), after analyzing the details of the company’s Apple Music streaming music subscription service.
Schachter finds that Apple Music, at 40 million users, is "likely the fastest growing contributor to Services revenues” for Apple.
However, it is not the biggest contributor to profit , he emphasizes. “Its margin profile (we are modeling 15%) is fundamentally different to the App Store (estimated 90% gross margin), and as such Music will likely never be a direct meaningful contributor to profits,” concludes Schachter.
By 2020, writes Schachter, “Music will contribute less than 4% of Services gross profit, versus apps at 56%.” He thinks investors shouldn’t be alarmed, but they should pay attention to the higher-profit App Store .
Apple Wants a Newsstand
Speaking of services, Apple is planning to add to its “Apple News” application with the addition of Texture , a startup Apple agreed last month to acquire, as a way to expand Apple’s subscription offerings beyond Apple Music, according to Mark Gurman and Gerry Smith of Bloomberg , citing multiple unnamed sources.
"A new, simplified subscription service covering multiple publications could spur Apple News usage and generate new revenue in a similar manner to the $9.99 per month Apple Music offering,” write the authors.
Apple shares today are up $1.72, or 1%, at $177.54.
Qualcomm’s Dim Future
Wireless technology giant Qualcomm ( QCOM ) is in trouble, according to a note this morning from Morgan Stanley’s James Faucette, in which he reiterates an Underweight rating on the stock.
On the plus side, he thinks it is likely China’s regulatory authority, MOFCOM , will approve the company’s pending acquisition of NXP Semiconductors ( NXPI ). It’s in China’s best interest, after all, he writes: "China is uniquely positioned to overcome the hurdles to 5G services, and securing Qualcomm's support will help Chinese OEMs capture market share of 5G handsets."
But after the deal, there’s a whole bunch of risks, including the ongoing lawsuit with Apple, which is “unlikely to conclude before fiscal 2019,” he believes. Another dispute, with China’s privately held phone maker Huawei , is also likely to persist, he writes. He thinks efforts by both Apple and Huawei to replace Qualcomm chips with their own parts will prompt smaller licensees of Qualcomm’s technology to resist paying royalties in future. And then there are challenges by Taiwanese chip maker MediaTek ( 2454TW ).
Qualcomm shares this morning are up 64 cents, or 1.2%, at $55.41.
